overall_safety_summary: The scene presents safety concerns regarding electrical hazards due to a power strip on the counter near wet food preparation, and physical hazards from improper knife grip technique.

hazards.description: A power strip with multiple plugs is located directly on the countertop next to the cutting board.
hazards.explanation: Spills or moisture from food preparation could seep into the electrical sockets, posing a risk of electrical shock or short circuit.
hazards.older_adult_relevance: Older adults may have slower physical responses to electrical emergencies or be more susceptible to severe injury from electrical shocks.
hazards.recommended_action: Relocate the power strip away from the food preparation area to a dry, elevated location.

hazards.description: The user is chopping onions while holding the vegetable with flat, extended fingers close to the knife blade.
hazards.explanation: This finger placement increases the risk of accidental cuts or lacerations if the knife slips.
hazards.older_adult_relevance: Age-related changes in skin thickness and slower healing times make lacerations more problematic for older adults.
hazards.recommended_action: Adopt a claw grip by curling the fingertips inward to guide the knife safely.

uncertainties: Whether the sandwich maker is currently hot or turned on.
